ben: quick report: running into weird exception chaining in the python sdk. when the transport raises a timeout we see a ClientTimeoutError from aiohttp wrapped inside APIError but the original exception isn't attached as __cause__ so traceback is useless.
ivy: can you paste the callsite?
ben: minimal async repro:```py
from redwood import RedwoodClient, APIError
client = RedwoodClient(api_key='...')
try:
    await client.chat.create(prompt='hello')
except APIError as e:
    print('status', getattr(e, 'status_code', None))
    # expected to inspect original transport error
    print('cause', getattr(e, '__cause__', None))
```
ben: Output shows APIError with status None and cause None; logs have "TimeoutError" from transport but it's not attached. also mypy can't import TimeoutError wrapper type because it isn't exported in errors.pyi.
john: ack. Two problems: (1) we drop original transport exceptions when creating APIError; (2) typeshed doesn't export transport/error helpers. Both matter for users who want to detect retryable network errors.
ivy: proposed fixes: a) when wrapping, use "raise APIError(...) from original_exc" to preserve __cause__; b) add attributes on APIError: .cause (Optional[str|Exception]) and .is_retryable() method that returns True for network timeouts and 5xx; c) export NamedError types in errors.pyi like TransportError, TimeoutError, AuthError so mypy can catch them.
ben: +1. Also request: include example in quickstart showing pattern for retries:```py
from redwood.errors import APIError, TimeoutError
try:
    await client.chat.create(...)
except TimeoutError:
    # exponential backoff
except APIError as e:
    if e.is_retryable():
        # backoff
    else:
        raise
```
docs: good call. we should show both sync and async examples. I'll add a short note about catching subclass exceptions vs checking e.is_retryable().
john: implementation notes: keep APIError base for backwards compatibility, make TransportError subclass it, and have TimeoutError subclass TransportError. Ensure exceptions are exported in package __init__ and in errors.pyi. Also ensure .raw_body/.parsed_body present for HTTP errors.
ivy: tests: unit that simulates raising transport.Timeout and assert "except TimeoutError" catches it; integration smoke that forces a socket timeout and checks e.__cause__ is instance of asyncio.TimeoutError. add mypy test that "from redwood.errors import TimeoutError" resolves.
ci-bot: Created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/issues/854 (py-sdk: preserve transport exception as __cause__ + export timeout/transport types in pyi)
ben: small DX ask: prefer that APIError.__str__ includes a short hint when __cause__ is present like "(cause: TimeoutError)" so logs are more helpful.
john: ok will add that. plan: create PR with runtime change, pyi update, tests, and docs snippet. target next patch release.
docs: i'll add quickstart snippet and migration note: "APIError now chains original transport exceptions and new concrete Transport/Timeout exception types are exported."
ben: thanks! saved me a lot of debugging time :thumbsup:
ci-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/721 (preserve transport cause on APIError + export timeout types)
ivy: assigning to @john. ping me for review.
ben: will validate once CI passes.
